hooks.text: Meteors fell across North America for nine hours straight.
Shooting stars were once thought to be simple weather.
Up to 240,000 meteors lit the night sky.

title: The Meteor Storm That Created Space Science
description: A historic meteor storm over North America in 1833 launched the modern science of meteors.

beats.text: Meteors fell across North America for nine hours straight.
beats.visual: Woodcut illustration of the 1833 Leonid meteor storm over North America, Adolf Vollmy

beats.text: Terrified onlookers feared the end of the world as stars fell like rain.
beats.visual: Leonid fireball meteor photograph, green fireball night sky

beats.text: At the time, scientists believed shooting stars were just atmospheric weather.
beats.visual: Meteoroid atmospheric entry illustration NASA, diagram showing meteor burning in atmosphere

beats.text: Yale professor Denison Olmsted noticed every meteor radiated from a single point.
beats.visual: Portrait of Yale professor Denison Olmsted, engraved portrait

beats.text: He proved meteors originated from a debris cloud in outer space.
beats.visual: Diagram of meteor shower radiant point in constellation Leo, sickle of Leo diagram
queries: Sickle of Leo meteor radiant diagram

beats.text: That terrifying storm launched the modern science of meteors.
